"Revolution" is very focused on violence and war as it is set in Kurdistan. Helly's mother had participated in Kurdish military struggles before they fled to Finland. Helly also wears the jamana/cemedani while in over-the-top military fatigues.

"Ez Kurdistan im" highlights Sehid Hozan Serhad, musician and fighter, who was killed in PKK-Turkey clashes in 1999. He was born in Sweden and wikipedia suggests that his parents migrated to Sweden in the 1970s. This would imply that his nuclear family had by and large avoided direct traumatic experiences unfolding in the 80s and 90s in Turkey. This video is set in the mountains, indicating the location of guerrilla warfare between Turkey and the PKK. He also wears the jamana/cemedani in this setting, indicative of political resistance.

"Take Me Home" is an outlier in these examples in that rather than fixating on virtualizing Kurdistan vis-a-vis the battlefield, they are toggling between childhood play/sense of innocence and adult nostalgia/revisiting of that time. Addressing Dashni in particular, much of her break into the entertainment industry was through television and acting, creating an almost Disney-like environment her creativity was funneled through. Some of her music that is too "Western" has also been negatively received.
